headline: WSJ, citing US officials, confirms the US attacked Qeshm Island on Monday as part of a secret limited-strikes campaign

sources: The Wall Street Journal, citing US officials (Alexander Ward, Lara Seligman, Shelby Holliday)
fault_line: Secret strike or air-defence interception: WSJ's US officials say America secretly hit Qeshm while Trump said 'we haven't been doing any fighting for months' -- and Iranian sources said the sounds were their defences dow

sections.what_happened: The US attacked Iran's Qeshm Island on Monday, US officials told the WSJ -- the latest in a series of limited strikes Washington has secretly carried out against Iran in recent weeks while Trump publicly touted a possible diplomatic deal. Some officials described the assaults as defensive, to prevent Iran having freedom to attack commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz; the campaign has deliberately not been publicly announced so as not to signal any intention of resuming major combat operations. The Defense Department referred questions to CENTCOM, which did not immediately respond. Trump told reporters Monday: 'We had a war with Iran. We won. I don't know if you even call it a war because we haven't been doing any fighting for months.' The WSJ also repeats its earlier reporting: CENTCOM chief Adm. Brad Cooper briefed Trump at the White House last week; CENTCOM has moved more missile defences and munitions into the region; the US has already told Gulf nations to prepare for a short and intense operation shortly after the election. Asked Monday if he was considering striking Iran after the midterms, Trump replied 'no', although administration officials said he was still weighing all options. This UPGRADES the Qeshm item: 0200-01 held the explosions as cause-unknown; 0300-02 held N12's US-strike attribution as single-source. The WSJ account now gives the strike attribution a second, major-outlet source with named reporters and multiple US officials behind it.
sections.what_verified: Two declared-tier families speak to the item: WSJ (T2) for the US-strike attribution, IRNA (T3, STATE IR) for the explosions themselves. N12's parallel US-strike account supports the same attribution but N12 has NO declared tier in the registry and is NOT counted. The two families do not independently confirm the same fact: IRNA confirms explosions, not attribution -- the attribution rests on WSJ's unnamed officials, stated explicitly here.
sections.what_disputed: No on-record US confirmation: CENTCOM did not respond to the WSJ, and the Pentagon has not announced the strikes. Iran has not confirmed a US strike on Qeshm: IRNA said only that the cause of the explosions was unknown, and Iranian sources relayed by Al Jazeera Mubasher (Nov 2, 21:35 UTC -- prior window, missed by the 0100 scan) said the sounds were air defences intercepting a US MQ-9 over Qeshm -- a competing explanation for the same sounds that the WSJ account does not address. Trump's own 'we haven't been doing any fighting for months' line sits in direct tension with a secret campaign his officials describe to the WSJ. The WSJ's 'short and intense operation shortly after the election' line is the same Gulf-warning reporting already recorded at 0400-01, not a new warning.
sections.why_matters: The secret war, confirmed by the WSJ: while Trump told voters 'we haven't been doing any fighting for months', US officials say America secretly struck Qeshm Island on Monday -- and has been striking for weeks without announcing it. The island guards Hormuz. The election is today. What comes after the vote?
